nodes.label: check() (start guard)
nodes.rationale: Until __mcBoot.ok: if the script never ran it reports an incomplete copy (no #mcEnd marker; the file is about 2.3 MB), a browser too old, or a load stopped by the browser; otherwise 'Still opening...' with the seconds and what it waits for, network-folder advice, and a recheck every 3 seconds.

nodes.label: esc() (start guard)
nodes.rationale: Escapes & < > " but not the single quote, enough for the element text it is used in; the main esc() in js/ui3.js, which the security skill relies on, also escapes '.

nodes.label: go() (start guard)
nodes.rationale: Runs on DOMContentLoaded and schedules the first check 1.5 seconds later, or 9 seconds more when the page's script already ran.

nodes.label: links() (start guard)
nodes.rationale: Writes Try again (reload) and, when the data folder is involved, Choose the data folder again, which calls window.__mcRepick defined by js/ui3.js.

nodes.label: window.__mcBoot (start-guard state)
nodes.rationale: { step, ran, ok, folder, errs }: window errors and unhandled rejections are noted (up to six); the app sets step and folder while it opens the data, ran when its script reaches the end, and ok when the first screen appears.

nodes.label: tooOld() (start guard)
nodes.rationale: Treats Internet Explorer, the old EdgeHTML Edge and Chrome or Edge before version 86 as too old for the tool.

nodes.label: Sign-in and lock dialog (#lock, #lockForm)
nodes.rationale: Sign-up and sign-in card: full name, username (3 to 32 characters, not the email, so it is harder to guess), I am (agent, supervisor, quality, WFM, senior manager), my supervisor, and password fields with a strength meter; #lockTitle, #lockSub, #lockErr and #lockLinks are also written by the start guard when the tool cannot start.

nodes.label: Opening the shared data
nodes.rationale: Choosing MC Data shows what the tool waits for with the seconds and, after 10 seconds, the usual causes (OneDrive or SharePoint files not on the computer: Always keep on this device; a network drive); slow, cancelled, refused or unreadable folders each say what to do, each file read gives up after 30 seconds, and a pill shows reading progress after sign-in.

nodes.label: theme_boot.html (#themeBoot: light or dark before the first paint)
nodes.norm_label: theme_boot.html (#themeboot: light or dark before the first paint)
nodes.rationale: Reads the mc-theme choice from localStorage (system by default), resolves System with prefers-color-scheme and sets data-theme on the page before the first paint; storage or matchMedia failures fall back without breaking the page.

nodes.label: App bar (#appbar)
nodes.rationale: Page title, Search, the reporting period menu, the bell with checks and notifications, How to use, Settings and the account menu with the System / Light / Dark appearance segment, Manage accounts, username and password changes, Lock now and Sign out.

nodes.label: Settings drawer (#dSettings)
nodes.rationale: Month, adherence target, NA cut-off, inactive days limit, Leave out people with no schedule, deduction scope, 100% adherence teams, attendance-template departments, logo, scorecards, the final form's manager, appearance and the auto-lock minutes.

nodes.label: Appearance setting (System / Light / Dark)
nodes.rationale: Chosen in the account menu, in Settings or with Search; kept in this browser as the mc-theme setting and applied before the first paint by js/theme_boot.html, with System following the computer. Apple's guidelines prefer no app-level setting; it is offered because it was asked for.

nodes.label: Leave out people with no schedule
nodes.norm_label: leave out people with no schedule
nodes.rationale: People the Schedule export has no day for and with no attendance are left out of every sheet, saved month and Excel export (named in the Overview and in Checks); teams set up with no Genesys data are never left out; a Settings switch, on by default, puts everyone back while the roster keeps everyone.

nodes.label: Brands' history (daily brand emails)
nodes.rationale: The shared history of the four brand emails (months and days) with Export history (member-care-history-<day>.json) and an Import history that shows the file first, adds missing months and days and keeps the tool's numbers unless told otherwise; it also reads the history built into the stand-alone Member Care Report Builder page (window.HISTORY_SEED).

nodes.label: Member Care Report Builder 14 (stand-alone daily report builder)
nodes.norm_label: member care report builder 14 (stand-alone daily report builder)
nodes.rationale: The earlier stand-alone page whose parts make the four daily brand emails; with dt/templates.js and dt/logos.js recreated with placeholders, the emails are not byte-identical until the originals are put back.

nodes.label: Parts the source document did not print
nodes.norm_label: parts the source document did not print
nodes.rationale: Encoded data left out of the restored markdown is recreated: js/fonts.css as Geist (originally Inter and Poppins), js/brand_src.html as an empty block (no company logo, so the neutral WF mark shows), dt/templates.js with 1x1 placeholder images, and dt/logos.js and dt/seed.js empty; dropping the originals back restores them byte for byte.

nodes.label: Recognise files drawer and drop overlay (#dRecog, #dropAll)
nodes.norm_label: recognise files drawer and drop overlay (#drecog, #dropall)
nodes.rationale: The panel that says what a dropped file is and where it goes, and the page-wide overlay 'Drop to recognise · nothing leaves this computer'.

nodes.label: Recognise files (one drop zone)
nodes.rationale: All the month's files go in one drop; each is identified on the computer from sheet names, columns, titles and dates (js/recog_core.js, in the parse worker) as Sure, Likely or Not sure, with its month and roster matches, and sent to the page that takes it. Nothing is uploaded and a choice is remembered by the shape of the columns only.

nodes.label: MC Performance Review deck
nodes.rationale: WFM team › Performance Review makes the Control and Complaint team's deck slide for slide from the MC performance Review email, the MC KPIs workbook, the Call history export (OTP and final termination calls counted per day and kept in config/calldays) and logos taken from a dropped deck (config/decklogos); js/prdeck.js reads and builds, js/perfrev.js is the page.

nodes.label: Weekly Commercial Presentation
nodes.rationale: WFM team › Weekly commercial makes the 7-slide VP deck and its Outlook draft in four steps: the month from the brands' history, the Call history and Tickets exports read in the browser, the outages list (config/outages), then the deck with real PowerPoint charts written without a library (js/pptx.js, js/wcdeck.js, js/weekly.js).

nodes.label: WFM team page
nodes.rationale: One page holding the month's build and the WFM tools as tabs: This month (Import, Review, Export, Emails), Every day (Daily, Report builder), Every week (Weekly commercial, Performance Review), Insight (Analytics, Agents, Interactions) and Keep (Data); each role sees its own tabs and each tab says what it needs.

nodes.label: Stakeholder deck (MC Monthly Report Builder - Overview.pptx)
nodes.norm_label: stakeholder deck (mc monthly report builder - overview.pptx)
nodes.rationale: 16 slides for the stakeholders and management in the tool's look, with speaker notes; the screenshots come from the synthetic test data and bash tools/deck/build.sh makes the deck again from the current build.

nodes.label: Attendance templates drawer (#dAttTpl)
nodes.rationale: Where each department's or supervisor's attendance template for a month is downloaded.

nodes.label: Emails view (#v-email)
nodes.rationale: Shared month or this build, for review or final, a message form (To, Cc, subject, deadline, greeting, sign-off and options such as Classic look) and a preview with Copy for Outlook, Download .eml, Save attachment and editing in the preview.

nodes.label: Export view (#v-export)
nodes.rationale: Builds the monthly workbook, the incentive data workbook and Smart-Link's attendance file, lists saved workbooks and the sheets, and explains what to do after the download.

nodes.label: Attendance templates per department
nodes.rationale: For departments whose supervisors take attendance by hand (TS, MG, CT, QA, DE, WF by default) js/atttpl.js makes one workbook per department and month, split by supervisor only when needed, with a How to fill sheet, exception rows only and checks that colour mistakes; CC and SM need none because their days come from the Genesys Schedule and Agent Status Timeline.

nodes.label: Corrections after the deduction email review
nodes.norm_label: corrections after the deduction email review
nodes.rationale: A box above the deduction email that reads corrections pasted, dropped (.msg, .eml, .xlsx, .csv) or typed one a line (js/updparse.js reads, js/attupd.js is the box); exceptions excuse lateness and conformance minutes, leaves change attendance, and Apply writes them as att/<month>/edits/<person> records marked src: 'update', with Undo.

nodes.label: Deduction and absences email
nodes.rationale: WFM team › Emails makes the month's deduction email for review and final from the shared month or a build; its attachment has only the Attendance Report and Monthly Deduction sheets and no ID column; the card-look Absenteeism table uses fixed widths, no wrapping and bgcolor so Outlook shows it whole.

nodes.label: Saved workbooks
nodes.rationale: Every build is kept as a locked copy with the shared data (repmeta/, repfile/); a plain copy in MC Data › MC Reports is off unless chosen in the build dialog, because anyone who can open the shared folder, agents too, could open it.

nodes.label: Smart-Link attendance file
nodes.rationale: Export builds the third party Smart-Link's monthly attendance workbook (Writer2.smartLink) for the agents on Smart-Link's own list (config/smartlink; without one, FRiENDi and FRiENDi Pay) with day codes, Tardy minutes and Smart-Link's own COUNTIF formulas; it is kept in Saved workbooks and goes to Smart-Link from Outlook.

nodes.label: Spreadsheet and CSV formula injection check (CWE-1236)
nodes.norm_label: spreadsheet and csv formula injection check (cwe-1236)
nodes.rationale: The xlsx writers (Writer2, WriterInc, atttpl) store data cells as strings and take formulas only from the tool's own constants; CSV text starting with = + - @, a tab or CR gets a leading apostrophe in rosterCsv (js/ui3.js) and exceptionsCsv (dt/wfm.js), and any new CSV writer must do the same.

nodes.label: Privacy check (National IDs, callers' numbers, synthetic fixtures)
nodes.norm_label: privacy check (national ids, callers' numbers, synthetic fixtures)
nodes.rationale: National IDs appear only where payroll needs them (Build's workbook and the roster) and never in email attachments (WriterInc noIds, Writer2.dedMail, withoutIds), plain shared files or team copies; callers' numbers (ANI) are never stored and the daily review's Mask customer numbers setting is off by default; fixtures use a first name and initial, made-up 10-digit IDs and example.com; records are never console.logged.

nodes.label: The tool sends nothing (Copy for Outlook / .eml drafts)
nodes.norm_label: the tool sends nothing (copy for outlook / .eml drafts)
nodes.rationale: Every email (daily brand emails, deduction, incentive, the weekly decks) is copied for Outlook or downloaded as an .eml draft and sent by a person, and files for third parties such as Smart-Link go from Outlook; the tool only records Copied or Downloaded with the time.

nodes.label: WFM team header, tabs and workspace (#wfmHead, #v-wfm)
nodes.norm_label: wfm team header, tabs and workspace (#wfmhead, #v-wfm)
nodes.rationale: Header with the month and Build Excel, the tab nav each role gets from wfmx.js, the vacation cover note and a view-only hint; the workspace section holds the report builder, daily emails, corrections and email panes.

nodes.label: Vacation cover
nodes.rationale: The WFM manager can tick an analyst on vacation to take their tabs and permissions, and an analyst can tick the manager; the tick is shared, says who and since when, is logged in cover/now and counts only while that account keeps its role.

nodes.label: One-to-one form, signature and objection drawers (#dForm, #dSign, #dObj)
nodes.norm_label: one-to-one form, signature and objection drawers (#dform, #dsign, #dobj)
nodes.rationale: Drawers where a one-to-one form is filled in, saved and downloaded as PDF, a final form is signed on screen, and an agent's objection is raised and answered.

nodes.label: Calculation engine (deductions and incentives)
nodes.rationale: The part every agent agrees survives: applying the company's rules to the two brands' Genesys exports and attendance to compute deductions, KPIs and incentives, released through existing approvers in the current template.

nodes.label: CIS Microsoft Edge Benchmark v4.0.0, item 1.4.6
nodes.norm_label: cis microsoft edge benchmark v4.0.0, item 1.4.6
nodes.rationale: Level 1 recommendation to block the write-permission request of the File System API, the browser feature the tool relies on to write the shared folder.

nodes.label: Saudi Electronic Transactions Law (signature validity)
nodes.rationale: Ties an electronic signature's legal standing to a digital certificate from a licensed authority, so the tool's drawn or typed one-to-one signature carries none and that work stays on paper.

nodes.label: File System Access API (Chromium-based Edge)
nodes.rationale: What makes 'one file with a data folder next to it' possible in Chromium-based Edge (the Believer's why-now), and the browser feature a CIS baseline recommends blocking (the Skeptic's risk).

nodes.label: Genesys Cloud WEM
nodes.rationale: Genesys's workforce engagement add-on (agent adherence widget, scorecards, coaching, quality evaluation disputes) the company likely already pays for (about 37,500 to 60,900 SAR a month for 250 agents), so rebuilding the employee and quality pages may mean paying twice.

nodes.label: NCA Essential Cybersecurity Controls (ECC 2-2-3-3, 2-12)
nodes.rationale: Least privilege and segregation of duties (2-2-3-3) and event logs (2-12), cited with the cloud controls (CCC) as gates any IT alternative or registered tool must pass.

nodes.label: Raymond Panko's spreadsheet-error research
nodes.rationale: Cited by the Believer for spreadsheet error rates (the often-quoted 88%) and turned by the Skeptic: programming errors resemble spreadsheet errors and individual review catches only about 63%.

nodes.label: Payroll acceptance gate
nodes.rationale: Payroll is the only gate that turns saved hours into value; asked, it accepts the deduction and incentive file when the senior manager sends it in an official email, which approves the sender rather than the calculation and makes the senior manager the sole reviewer.

nodes.label: Reconciliation with the manual Excel
nodes.rationale: The built-in comparison of the tool's results with the Excel files prepared the old way; the council warns it proves imitation rather than correctness when every difference is closed by changing the tool, and requires an untuned month where each difference is classified as a tool error, an Excel error or an unwritten rule.

nodes.label: Role pages (employee page, signature, objection, approval)
nodes.norm_label: role pages (employee page, signature, objection, approval)
nodes.rationale: The multi-role layer the Judge first froze and the re-judge ruled to delete until legal and cybersecurity agree in writing, since it turns the calculator into a parallel identity system that cybersecurity could shut down together with the engine; the November 2026 README still documents the agent's page, signed one-to-one forms, objections and Finalize.

nodes.label: Saudi Labor Law, Articles 66-72 (Article 72 amendment, February 2025)
nodes.norm_label: saudi labor law, articles 66-72 (article 72 amendment, february 2025)
nodes.rationale: Disciplinary rules (repetition within 180 days, the 30-day limit, a cap of five days' wage deduction, notice and a hearing); the amended Article 72 gives 30 days for a written grievance and 15 days for a decision before the labour court.

nodes.label: Saudi Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL)
nodes.rationale: Binding since 14 September 2024, with a transfer regulation that requires a risk assessment before personal data leaves the Kingdom; fines reach 5 million SAR.

nodes.label: Council memory (council.md)
nodes.rationale: The claude-council verdict memory (in Arabic): for 2026-10-19 MC Report Builder (internal) it keeps each agent's position and key claim, the Judge's FIX FIRST with its de-risk call, and the re-judge (FIX FIRST unchanged) with payroll's answer and the claims that survived two sittings.

nodes.label: Council session 2026-10-19: MC Report Builder (internal)
nodes.rationale: Full four-agent council record (in Arabic) on the internal tool of a Saudi telecom's Member Care department: the idea, the Believer, the Skeptic, the coordinator's facts from the code, the Investor, the Judge's verdict and a re-judge after payroll's answer.

nodes.label: Believer case: manual close costs about 140 h a month, the tool recovers 70%
nodes.norm_label: believer case: manual close costs about 140 h a month, the tool recovers 70%
nodes.rationale: The WFM analyst's manual close (Genesys exports, VLOOKUP ID matching, per-brand formulas, Outlook messages one by one, objections, daily reports) and supervisors' one-to-one paperwork cost about 140 hours a month (assumptions: 250 agents, 18 supervisors, 100 SAR an hour, about 14,000 SAR); the tool would recover 70% with no licence or server, and reconciling the last three months plus timing one close proves it this week.

nodes.label: Investor case: a time-allocation decision; the engine alone returns about 2.8 to 1
nodes.norm_label: investor case: a time-allocation decision; the engine alone returns about 2.8 to 1
nodes.rationale: Almost no cash moves either way, so this is time allocation: the decision owner (the senior manager) does not feel the pain, the analyst who does has no say, and payroll carries the risk. The return swings from 2.9 to 0.9 to 1 on two items, one-to-ones (63 h, waiting on legal's view of the signature) and Outlook messages (17 h, free alternative); the engine alone gives about 2.8 to 1 at a quarter of the maintenance. The company probably already pays for Genesys WEM, and the builder's time went to look and motion, not identity or audit.

nodes.label: Judge verdict: FIX FIRST
nodes.rationale: Strongest argument the Investor's, weakest the Believer's, the Skeptic right in substance though wrong that the page cannot know its user. Biggest risk: the tool never becomes payroll's official source because payroll was never asked. De-risk: a five-minute call asking payroll whether the October file, in the current template from the senior manager's email but computed by an internal tool, would be entered as is. Fix: cut to the calculation engine and the reconciliation tool, prove correctness on an untuned month with every difference classified by cause, freeze the employee, signature, objection and approval pages, and keep real staff files out of AI sessions.

nodes.label: Re-judge: FIX FIRST unchanged (delete the role pages)
nodes.norm_label: re-judge: fix first unchanged (delete the role pages)
nodes.rationale: New evidence: payroll will accept the file if it comes from the senior manager in an official email, and the founder notes the tool computes earned incentives, not payroll. The verdict holds because payroll's yes moved the risk to the senior manager as the only reviewer while Excel stays the yardstick. De-risk: ask the senior manager which number leaves his email when tool and Excel differ, and when manual Excel stops. Fix: delete (not freeze) the role pages, release no file before the tool passes an untuned month with each difference traced to Genesys or the attendance sheet, and keep real staff files out of AI.

nodes.label: Skeptic case: the engine survives as a calculator, the multi-role system does not
nodes.norm_label: skeptic case: the engine survives as a calculator, the multi-role system does not
nodes.rationale: Payroll, cybersecurity and legal will not accept the tool's identity, signature and non-independent log as a payroll input, so Excel runs in parallel until the tool is abandoned; a page on a shared folder cannot know who uses it, stop others editing or prove what happened. Named risks: unregistered software, File System API writes a CIS baseline blocks, XSS reviewed by no one but the builder, signatures without legal standing, and real personal data passing through AI maintenance.

nodes.label: No real staff files in AI sessions
nodes.norm_label: no real staff files in ai sessions
nodes.rationale: Maintaining the tool with AI on real files would move personal data out of the Kingdom under the PDPL transfer rules, so the Investor's free control, made a condition by both verdicts, is that only synthetic test files are used in maintenance.

nodes.label: Incentive email (Supervisors › Incentive email)
nodes.rationale: The senior manager's email of the incentive data to the champions, for review and then final; its attachment is the incentive file the WFM analysts build, kept with the shared data and sent without the ID column; the final keeps the old body and what changed is shown only to the sender.

nodes.label: Every page in the order the month is done
nodes.norm_label: every page in the order the month is done
nodes.rationale: Pages that hold a month's work show numbered steps (the senior manager's month close in eight, Quality in six) or numbered tabs (WFM team 1-4, a supervisor's Team 1-3), each saying when it is done and marking the next, with look-up and set-once sections after; sidebars and quick actions follow the same order, and test/steps.cjs checks every role.

nodes.label: How this was counted drawer (#dHow)
nodes.rationale: Shows one person's KPI values, bands, ranks and points, the days and the eligibility checks behind a Final %.

nodes.label: How it is counted (counting rules and per-person explanation)
nodes.norm_label: how it is counted (counting rules and per-person explanation)
nodes.rationale: The rules drawer section for scheduled and late days, the absence penalty, minimum days, KPIs with no value, band edges, ranking and Final % rounding, whole SR and critical errors; percent KPIs and the Final % are rounded half up to a whole % by default as the old incentive files did, while the days % never is; Months in the job (6 by default) and the absence penalty decide eligibility; every person has a How this was counted breakdown.

nodes.label: Sandboxed email preview iframe (#mailFrame)
nodes.rationale: <iframe sandbox="allow-same-origin"> without allow-scripts; ui3.js writes the email into its srcdoc, so markup planted in an email body cannot run script.

nodes.label: Injection into the page check (OWASP A03, CWE-79)
nodes.norm_label: injection into the page check (owasp a03, cwe-79)
nodes.rationale: Every data value reaching innerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML or an HTML template literal goes through esc() (js/ui3.js, or a dt/*.js module's own esc), which covers & < > " ' and so is right in element text and quoted attributes; URL attributes take only tool-built data:, blob: or #id values; previews render in <iframe sandbox="allow-same-origin"> via srcdoc, never allow-scripts; no eval, new Function, string setTimeout or javascript: URLs. test/xss.cjs plants HTML in every name and opens every page for all seven roles.

nodes.label: Manage accounts drawer (#dAccounts)
nodes.rationale: How people sign in (username or email), the account list, Data from before (copy what this browser kept into the shared folder; older accounts keep their password and their access opens the next time an admin opens the tool), Download team copy and the roles list; auth.js runs autoGrants when it opens.

nodes.label: Tool roles (Admin, WFM analyst, WFM manager, Senior manager, Supervisor, Quality team, Agent, Waiting for access)
nodes.norm_label: tool roles (admin, wfm analyst, wfm manager, senior manager, supervisor, quality team, agent, waiting for access)
nodes.rationale: Admin manages accounts; the WFM analyst builds the month and the daily emails without seeing incentive amounts; the WFM manager sends the brand, deduction and absence emails; the senior manager sets scorecards, deadlines and incentive rules, sends the incentive emails and finalizes the month; a supervisor runs the team's one-to-ones, attendance and objections; the quality team drops the Final EVAL; an agent sees only their own page; new sign-ups wait for access.

nodes.label: Manage accounts
nodes.rationale: Lists every account record in the data, old ones with no username too, with a search box, role chips and Edit; access records left without an account and account files that cannot be read are listed under Records with no account and can be removed.

nodes.label: MC Data shared folder
nodes.rationale: The folder next to the HTML in the common folder that holds the shared data: plain account files, locked records such as att/<month>/edits/<person>, cover/now, config/*, ksrc/<month>, locked saved uploads (upmeta/, upfile/) and saved workbooks (repmeta/, repfile/), plus an opt-in plain copy in MC Reports.

nodes.label: Browser test suite (synthetic people)
nodes.rationale: Playwright scripts that use only synthetic people (first name and initial, made-up IDs, example.com addresses) across every role, theme and screen size, plus npm test's Node checks; pages load with the test hooks window.__NOLOCK__, window.__ROSTER__ and window.__mcUser, which auth.js honours only when there is no data store and sign-in is off.

nodes.label: Trust in the shared folder check (CWE-345, CWE-269)
nodes.norm_label: trust in the shared folder check (cwe-345, cwe-269)
nodes.rationale: Access is never taken from plain files: builtIn is dropped when accounts are read (listRaw), roles come from the encrypted staff-only dir/* through effective()/peopleAll() in js/auth.js, and a team copy's built-in admins come from peopleAll(); backup import refuses accounts, meta, akeys and dir records. test/trust.cjs plants a "builtIn": true account and a "role": "admin" account and checks neither gets the data key, a role, a Built-in/Admin label or a place in a team copy.

nodes.label: MC threat model (insider with access to the shared folder)
nodes.norm_label: mc threat model (insider with access to the shared folder)
nodes.rationale: Assets: names, National IDs and results in AES-GCM records; passwords as PBKDF2-SHA256 hashes (600 000 rounds, 16-byte salt) in plain accounts/* files; the team data key wrapped with RSA-OAEP-2048; agent keys in akeys/*; the tool's HTML. Layers: plain files in MC Data are writable by anyone with the folder so access never comes from their fields; roles among staff are tool rules, not cryptography; the HTML's integrity rests on folder permissions; the online page encrypts nothing; uploaded files are untrusted.

nodes.label: Coordinator's facts from the tool's code
nodes.norm_label: coordinator's facts from the tool's code
nodes.rationale: The tool has its own username and password accounts with seven roles granted by an admin; shared data files are AES-GCM encrypted with keys locked by each person's password (PBKDF2), staff open the team key and an agent only their own data; manual edits are logged with account and time but inside the data, not as an independent audit log; identity is the tool's, not the company's (no Active Directory or SSO); signatures are drawn or typed, not certificate-based; anyone who can delete in the folder can delete files.

nodes.label: Fixed (high): planted builtIn / role in account files
nodes.norm_label: fixed (high): planted builtin / role in account files
nodes.rationale: Account files in MC Data are plain files anyone with the folder can write; a file saying "builtIn": true got the team's data key and the admin role at the next admin sign-in, and a planted "role": "admin" became a built-in admin of the next team copy. Built in now comes only from the team copy's own settings, and team-copy admins from the staff-only directory.

nodes.label: brand_src.html (#brand-assets JSON)
nodes.rationale: An empty JSON block: no company logo is built in, so ui3.js's BRAND is null and the neutral WF mark shows unless a logo is chosen in Settings; the original carried the Beyond One logos.

nodes.label: csp_boot.html (#cspBoot no-network Content-Security-Policy)
nodes.rationale: Opened from file:, it appends a meta Content-Security-Policy default-src 'unsafe-inline' data: blob:; form-action 'none'; base-uri 'none', so the browser refuses any web address and no mistake or planted text could send the data anywhere; the online page keeps the rules of the site that serves it.

nodes.label: head_boot.html (start guard)
nodes.rationale: Plain old JavaScript on purpose so it runs in any browser: when the tool has not shown its first screen a few seconds after load, the sign-in card says why (an incomplete copy, a browser too old, a stopped load, or what it still waits for) instead of 'Loading...' for ever.

nodes.label: ui3_body.html (app body markup)
nodes.rationale: Static body of the single-page tool: the icon sprite, the sign-in card, sidebar, app bar, the Build and WFM views, the role workspaces, drawers and dialogs; the assemble scripts put it after the head and the team copy re-serializes it.

nodes.label: Workspace sidebar (#sidebar, #wsSeg)
nodes.rationale: Search at the top, the workspace buttons shown per role (Dashboard, Build, Team, Results, Supervisors, WFM team, Quality, My page), How to use, Settings and the rail toggle; the brand images #blDark and #blLight sit at its top next to the WF mark.

nodes.label: Online page (out/mc-report-builder.html)
nodes.rationale: The variant assemble3.sh builds for a host with the window.claude data store; it keeps its host's rules instead of the file:// CSP, and per the threat model nothing is encrypted there and roles are only a convenience.

nodes.label: No-network rule check
nodes.rationale: Opened as a file, the page gets default-src 'unsafe-inline' data: blob:; form-action 'none'; base-uri 'none' from js/csp_boot.html, the first script in the head, and everything it uses is inline, data: or blob:; never add a <link>, <script src>, fetch or image pointing to a web address, and fonts stay data: in fonts.css. test/xss.cjs checks web requests are refused and test/supply.cjs that the built page names no web address and the rule comes first.

nodes.label: Node.js CI workflow (node.js.yml)
nodes.rationale: GitHub Actions workflow named Node.js CI that runs on push and pull_request to the branch claude/build-request-nj4kyb.

nodes.label: CI build job (Node 18.x / 20.x / 22.x matrix)
nodes.rationale: Runs on ubuntu-latest for each Node version: checkout, setup-node with the npm cache, then npm ci, npm run build --if-present and npm test.

nodes.label: actions/checkout@v4
nodes.rationale: Third-party action pinned by its major tag, not a commit SHA; the security skill asks for a full commit SHA pin when it is updated.

nodes.label: actions/setup-node@v4
nodes.rationale: Third-party action with the npm cache, pinned by its major tag, not a commit SHA; the security skill asks for a full commit SHA pin when it is updated.

nodes.label: Build pipeline (combine.py, assemble scripts, npm run build)
nodes.norm_label: build pipeline (combine.py, assemble scripts, npm run build)
nodes.rationale: python3 combine.py writes the main script (checked with node --check), assemble_standalone.sh writes the common-folder file and assemble3.sh the online page; npm run build runs the three steps into out/mc.html and npm test runs the Node-only checks, both on every push in GitHub Actions; tools/build_fonts.py rebuilds js/fonts.css with only Python.

nodes.label: Supply chain check
nodes.rationale: Nothing comes from npm at run time (package.json has no dependencies); GSAP is vendored and pinned by SHA-256 in vendor/README.md (test/supply.cjs); fonts are built from tools/fontsrc (SIL OFL); the CI workflow has permissions: contents: read and actions/checkout and actions/setup-node should be pinned to a full commit SHA when updated; tools/deck installs pptxgenjs@3.12.0 only to make the stakeholder deck.

nodes.label: Read-only CI token (permissions: contents: read)
nodes.rationale: The job only reads the code, so its token cannot push, open releases or change settings; the security review records this as a supply-chain control and npm test checks it.

nodes.label: Claude Code Cybersecurity Skills (Riyan Pratama / Masriyan, MIT)
nodes.norm_label: claude code cybersecurity skills (riyan pratama / masriyan, mit)
nodes.rationale: Upstream pack (github.com/Masriyan/Claude-Code-CyberSecurity-Skill, commit 3aa77d8) adapted under the MIT License with attribution: the evidence contract, 09 web security (context-by-context injection, header review, finding shape), 13 crypto analysis (checklist, precision rule), 20 supply chain, 02 vulnerability scanner (CVSS) and 19 GRC (risk register). Offensive material, payloads and scripts were left out; the modified version is not endorsed by the original author.

nodes.label: Team data key
nodes.rationale: One AES-GCM key for all staff records, wrapped with RSA-OAEP-2048 for each staff account's public key inside that account's file; every staff account can read and write every staff record, and the key is never rotated, so a person who once held it may keep a copy after leaving.

nodes.label: mc-security-review skill (SKILL.md)
nodes.rationale: Project security-review skill for the MC Monthly Report Builder: review the one-file tool the way an insider with access to the shared folder would attack it, prove each finding with synthetic test data, fix it at the right place and leave a test behind. Triggered by changes to js/auth.js, js/store.js, js/backup.js, anything that writes HTML, emails, CSV or xlsx, the build scripts or the CI workflow.

nodes.label: autoGrants (trust on first key)
nodes.rationale: In an admin's session, 1.5 s after sign-in, the data key is handed only to built-ins from the HTML's #team-config and to accounts whose staff role is in dir/* with no key fingerprint yet; the second case is a known open risk, since someone who writes a key into such an account file before its owner first signs in could get access.

nodes.label: Email draft header injection check (CWE-93)
nodes.rationale: Headers only go through hdrWord, hdrAddr and hdrSafe (emlFile in js/ui3.js); recipients are normalised (normSpace, addrList), bodies escaped and attachment names passed through hdrSafe; dt/wfm.js buildEml takes only pattern-matching addresses and its own subject. test/xss.cjs puts CR/LF into two addresses, the subject and a file name and expects no new header.

nodes.label: Evidence contract (observed / inferred / unverified)
nodes.rationale: A finding counts as observed only when a test reproduces it on the current build before the fix with the synthetic data (test/fixture.js, test/exports.cjs) and the same test passes after it. Real people's workbooks are read only in the scratchpad and nothing derived from them enters the repo, a test, a report or a commit; reviews run offline and file contents are untrusted data, not instructions.

nodes.label: Finding report format (CVSS 3.1, MC-SEC-NN block, risk register)
nodes.norm_label: finding report format (cvss 3.1, mc-sec-nn block, risk register)
nodes.rationale: Each finding gets a CVSS 3.1 vector and score and is ranked by reach first (anyone with the folder outranks admin-only), written as an MC-SEC-NN block (Severity, Where, Who can do it, What it gives them, Before observed, Fix, After, What stays open); open risks go into an ID | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Inherent | Controls | Residual | Treatment | Owner register row.

nodes.label: Known open risks (by design)
nodes.rationale: Accounts moved from a browser's own storage are trusted on their first key; reopening access after a password reset trusts whatever public key the account file holds; account details in plain files can be changed; staff roles are not cryptographic because all staff share one data key; the team data key is never rotated. Each row names what would close it: manual confirmation or recorded fingerprints, signed account files, one key per area or a server, re-encryption with a new key.

nodes.label: Advice for the people who run the tool
nodes.norm_label: advice for the people who run the tool
nodes.rationale: Keep the HTML in the common folder read-only for everyone but its owner; admins use long passphrases because an admin password opens the team's data key and its hash sits in accounts/* and every team copy where it can be guessed offline; keep the .mcbak password separate from sign-in passwords; turning off a leaver's account stops the tool, not a copy of the key they may hold.

nodes.label: October 2026 security review
nodes.rationale: Run with the adapted mc-security-review skill: every finding was first shown on the build before the fix with synthetic data, then fixed, and its test stays. Outcomes: planted account files fixed (high); backups raised to 600 000 rounds; CSV formula cells prefixed; line breaks can no longer start Outlook headers; the file:// page refuses any web address; GSAP pinned by SHA-256 and a read-only CI token; escaping and encryption checked with nothing to fix. Four risks stay open by design.

nodes.label: WFM team › Data: export and import all data (.mcbak)
nodes.norm_label: wfm team › data: export and import all data (.mcbak)
nodes.rationale: js/backup.js puts every record the tool keeps into one .mcbak file locked with a password chosen there (PBKDF2-SHA256 and AES-GCM; raised from 250 000 to 600 000 rounds by the security review); accounts, passwords and keys are never in it; import shows what is inside by kind and replaces only the same records.

nodes.label: Cryptography review (PBKDF2-SHA256, AES-GCM-256, RSA-OAEP-2048)
nodes.rationale: PBKDF2-SHA256 with at least 600 000 rounds (OWASP) and a 16-byte random salt for sign-in and backups (a backup states its own count; 100 000 to 5 000 000 accepted); AES-GCM-256 with a fresh 96-bit IV per seal and the record path plus key tag as AAD so records cannot be moved; RSA-OAEP-2048/SHA-256 key wrapping, noted as on the post-quantum clock; crypto.getRandomValues for keys, salts and IVs. Precision rule: every crypto finding names primitive, key size, mode, rounds and the concrete upgrade. Verified by test/datafolder.cjs.

nodes.label: apple-design-skill (dickwu)
nodes.rationale: github.com/dickwu/apple-design-skill, the review of Apple's Human Interface Guidelines that the Option A design follows.

nodes.label: MC Monthly Report Builder (offline HTML tool)
nodes.norm_label: mc monthly report builder (offline html tool)
nodes.rationale: The Member Care Workforce Management tool: one offline HTML file, opened in Edge or Chrome from the common folder next to the MC Data folder, that turns the month's Genesys Cloud exports and the supervisors' attendance sheets into the monthly report, the incentive data, KPI results, one-to-ones, objections, the month close and the daily reports. There is no server; it sends nothing and makes no network request.

nodes.label: v33 source (restored from MC Monthly Report Builder.md, Part 2)
nodes.norm_label: v33 source (restored from mc monthly report builder.md, part 2)
nodes.rationale: Every calculation, output, email template, role, permission and storage format is the same as v33 by default; new counting settings start at what v33 did and tests compare 10,000 synthetic people against the v33 code (test/ref).

nodes.label: Geist typeface (The Geist Project Authors)
nodes.rationale: Copyright 2024 The Geist Project Authors (github.com/vercel/geist-font); its latin subset is embedded in js/fonts.css as data: for the tool's titles and numbers.

nodes.label: SIL Open Font License 1.1
nodes.rationale: Lets the font be used, studied, modified, embedded and redistributed with software as long as it is not sold by itself, each copy carries the copyright notice and licence, Reserved Font Names are not used by derivatives and derivatives stay under the OFL.

nodes.label: GSAP 3.15.0 (GreenSock)
nodes.rationale: gsap.min.js copied unchanged from its npm package (sourceMappingURL removed) under GreenSock's standard no-charge licence and inlined by the assemble scripts so the page needs no network; js/motion.js uses it only for phone drawer and More-sheet swipes, the dashboard count-up and growing progress bars, none of it with reduced motion. Lenis smooth scrolling was taken out with the Option A design.

nodes.label: README.md (MC Monthly Report Builder)
nodes.rationale: Project README: what the tool is, the Option A and glass design, every round of additions from October and November 2026, the security review, how to build and how to test.

nodes.label: GEIST-OFL.txt (Geist font licence)
nodes.rationale: Copyright notice of the Geist font and the full SIL Open Font License 1.1 text, kept next to the font source as the licence requires.

nodes.label: vendor/README.md (third-party code built into the page)
nodes.norm_label: vendor/readme.md (third-party code built into the page)
nodes.rationale: Records the vendored library, its licence, what the page uses it for and the reviewed update procedure.

nodes.label: Glass (glassmorphism) layer
nodes.rationale: Since 27 October 2026 the interface is frosted glass over a still field of colour in js/ui6/97_glass.css, loaded last so removing the file brings back the design underneath; no glass on glass, so nested panels are fills and text stays sharp; sticky table headers are nearly solid; Reduce transparency, Increase contrast and printing turn surfaces solid.

nodes.label: Motion (D9): still for everyday work
nodes.rationale: Nothing moves on what is done many times a day; pages rise in on first view, the dashboard counts up once a visit and progress bars grow from where they were; on a phone a drawer or the More sheet follows the finger and closes by speed and distance (GSAP, Apple's momentum projection); reduced motion turns movement into 120 ms fades.

nodes.label: Option A (Daylight) design by Apple's Human Interface Guidelines
nodes.norm_label: option a (daylight) design by apple's human interface guidelines
nodes.rationale: Chosen from three samples and built by Apple's HIG as the apple-design-skill reviews them: system grey with white 16 px cards, Apple's status colours with orange kept for the main action, contrast-checked text, Geist for titles and numbers, a sidebar with a 72 px icon rail and a phone tab bar (D1), title-style capitalization on screen (js/caps.js), blur only on floating layers and alternating table rows.

nodes.label: SHA-256 pin of the reviewed gsap.min.js
nodes.norm_label: sha-256 pin of the reviewed gsap.min.js
nodes.rationale: Updating means npm pack, copying dist/gsap.min.js, reading what changed and recording the new SHA-256 (currently 92bb9a96476f983d212a2bc4f54c889039c1696dd4461d40a736860938570fbb); npm test (test/supply.cjs) fails while the file and the recorded hash differ, so a changed library is always a deliberate, reviewed step.

nodes.label: Role workspace views (#v-dash, #v-team, #v-results, #v-cycle, #v-quality, #v-me, #v-wait, #v-blocked)
nodes.rationale: Containers for the Dashboard, a supervisor's Team, Results with Finalize, the senior manager's Supervisors month close with its incentive email pane, Quality results, the agent's My page where one-to-ones are filled in and signed, Waiting for access, and 'Not one of your pages' for pages another role owns.

nodes.label: Dashboard (D2, D6)
nodes.rationale: First page of the admin, WFM analyst, WFM manager and senior manager: greeting, quick actions, six KPI cards with the change against last month and a sparkline, the senior manager's month-close steps, the trend chart, what needs attention, the lowest adherence and data status, built only from data the tool already had.

nodes.label: Quality page (Final EVAL template)
nodes.rationale: One table per team (Call QA, Ticket QA / Empowerment Utilization, Call Reason & FCR Accuracy, Final Score); Call QA is Quality Observations in the scorecards (CT uses the Final Score); DRC-CSAT is one box that counts for every agent whose scorecard has it; the EVAL template downloads with IDs.

nodes.label: KPI scorecards drawer (#dScore)
nodes.rationale: KPIs, weights, ranking bands and the incentive base per team; changes apply straight away and are saved with the tool.

nodes.label: CT team's incentive workbook import
nodes.rationale: WFM team › Import reads the CT workbook's per-day blocks (Core.parseDayBlocks): attendance codes matched to the roster by the workbook's own National ID list, and Utilization ((ticket hours + other hours) / 7, averaged) kept in ksrc/<month>, where the KPI file's value wins and a typed value wins over both; it is no longer taken for the HR IDs file.

nodes.label: Every department's scorecard
nodes.rationale: Scorecards follow the September 2026 incentive file: CC, SM, CT, the QA and WF specialists, TS, DE and OP, plus one-role cards (OP-DIG, CT-SPV, CT-CCM, CT-SGM, QA-MGR, WF-MGR, DE-MGR); Team Performance is the supervised people's average final %, month figures are typed once per brand, values typed by hand win, NA ranks 5, and a card can have its own base per brand.

nodes.label: How to use drawer (#dHelp)
nodes.rationale: In-app guide: each department's steps, getting around, every month's steps, where each Genesys Cloud export is found and what it fills, the counting rules, roles and pages, closing a month, objections, coaching follow-up, incentive rules, reconcile, search, the shared folder, accounts and Your data (files are read on the computer and never sent).

nodes.label: Import view (#v-import)
nodes.rationale: One drop zone for all of the month's files, the four Genesys export slots, the attendance, IDs and KPI cards, saved uploads, and a side panel with what the workbook needs and a session-only import log whose files are never sent anywhere.

nodes.label: Review view (#v-review)
nodes.rationale: Tabs Checks (summary, filter tiles, build readiness), Issues, People (roster as cards or table, duplicates, Match system names, Supervisors, roster import and export), KPI results, Preview and History.

nodes.label: Build workflow: Import, Review (Checks), Export, Emails
nodes.norm_label: build workflow: import, review (checks), export, emails
nodes.rationale: The month's steps as numbered tabs of the WFM team page: Import (what the workbook needs, a session-only import log, saved uploads), Review opening on Checks with the three real build blockers, Build the Workbook with an honest confirmation ('Nothing was sent or uploaded'), and email steps recorded as Copied or Downloaded.

nodes.label: Genesys Cloud exports (Monthly Adherence, Agent Performance Summary, Schedule, Agent Status Timeline)
nodes.norm_label: genesys cloud exports (monthly adherence, agent performance summary, schedule, agent status timeline)
nodes.rationale: The month's exports dropped on Import that the report is built from; the Schedule and Agent Status Timeline also give CC and SM attendance without sheets, and an Interactions export feeds the WFM analytics.

nodes.label: Reconcile with the old Excel
nodes.rationale: Results › Reconcile takes up to three old workbooks (final result, incentive data, deduction) or a pasted results table, lines people up by national ID then by name, and groups every difference by its cause (js/recon.js); the senior manager or an admin fixes the cause (Use these bases, Use this rule) or takes the old value as a logged adjustment, each with Undo.

nodes.label: Saved uploads
nodes.rationale: Every Genesys export and attendance sheet dropped on Import is kept as dropped under the month of its own rows: locked in the data folder (upmeta/, upfile/), with the online page's data, or in IndexedDB; after a sign-out or reload the latest month is back in Build, and files can be moved, replaced or deleted with Undo.

hyperedges.label: Offline guarantee: everything inline, nothing over the network
Synthetic-data-only policy (council condition, security evidence contract, privacy rules, test suite)
Page head boot sequence assembled by make_head.py (CSP first, theme before first paint, start guard on the sign-in card)
